title: [Advisory] PHP: Multiple Critical Vulnerabilities
content:
##### SEVERITY AND IMPACT:
- Successful exploitation allows unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary code with PHP worker privileges via crafted HTTP requests, and local attackers to escalate to root through PHP-FPM.
- **Current exploitation status**: UNKNOWN (the vendor reports working exploit chains in testing, but no public PoC is referenced)

##### AFFECTED PRODUCTS:
- PHP (The PHP Group): engine, PHP-FPM, PHP-CGI, LSAPI, Apache mod_php, and the session and date extensions
- Deployments fronted by nginx, Apache (mod_proxy_fcgi) or HAProxy that reuse FastCGI backend connections
- Official PHP-FPM Docker images, which enable `catch_workers_output`
- For specific versions, please check the references.

##### VULNERABILITY DETAILS:
- **Attack Chain:**
    - CVE-2026-129289: Malformed multipart bodies leave unread `php://input` bytes on a reused FastCGI connection. These bytes form a forged request that sets `auto_prepend_file=php://input`, giving remote code execution.
    - CVE-2026-129291: Code running in a worker escalates to root through an epoll use-after-free in the FPM master.
- **Prerequisites:**
    - Request smuggling: front-end connection reuse (`fastcgi_keep_conn on` or `enablereuse=on`) and an application path that opens `php://input` without fully reading it.
    - Use-after-free and session flaws: specific configurations, namely fatal error backtraces with arguments, file-based error logging with startup diagnostics, session upload progress or mismatched serializers, and gadget chains.
- **Impact Details:**
    - Request smuggling bypasses front-end routing, spoofs `REMOTE_ADDR`, and can leave admin-level INI settings active for later requests.
    - The FPM epoll flaw yields root command execution when the FPM master runs as root.
- **Available Mitigations:**
    - Vendor patches are available for all supported PHP branches. Upgrade immediately.
    - **Temporary:**
        - Disable FastCGI backend connection reuse: nginx `fastcgi_keep_conn`, Apache `enablereuse`, or the HAProxy equivalent.
        - Set `zend.exception_ignore_args=1` and/or `fatal_error_backtraces=0` in the effective FPM and Apache configuration, then restart workers.
        - Set `session.upload_progress.enabled=0` administratively.
        - Use a consistent `session.serialize_handler` across everything that shares a session store.
        - Fix configuration errors that produce startup diagnostics, or log PHP errors to syslog.
        - Disable `catch_workers_output` in FPM pools.
        - Set `pm.max_requests=1` in PHP-FPM, accepting the performance cost.
        - Never expose PHP-FPM or LSAPI listeners to untrusted networks.

##### CVEs IN THIS ADVISORY:
Numeric CVSS scores were not published in the referenced advisories. Ratings below are vendor-assigned, ordered by severity and exploitability.
- CVE-2026-129289 CVSS4.0: (CRITICAL) - PHP-FPM request smuggling via unread request body leading to unauthenticated RCE
- CVE-2026-129182 CVSS4.0: (CRITICAL) - Use-after-free through a fatal-error backtrace repopulated after shutdown, potential RCE
- CVE-2026-126714 CVSS4.0: (CRITICAL) - Interrupted session file writes enable object injection and RCE
- CVE-2026-129474 CVSS4.0: (CRITICAL) - Use-after-free in `__call`/`__callStatic` backtraces, confirmed RCE
- CVE-2026-129496 CVSS4.0: (CRITICAL) - Timezone cache use-after-free during worker startup, RCE demonstrated in FPM and mod_php
- CVE-2026-115560 CVSS4.0: (CRITICAL) - Session serializer mismatch via upload progress, RCE using Guzzle/Monolog gadgets
- CVE-2026-129481 CVSS4.0: (CRITICAL) - Use-after-free after interrupted session shutdown in reused workers
- CVE-2026-129291 CVSS4.0: (HIGH) - PHP-FPM epoll use-after-free, local privilege escalation to root
- CVE-2026-109619 - Earlier related stale-global-state use-after-free; the fix was incomplete and is addressed by the above

##### REFERENCES:
Primary:
- Source Advisory: https://www.php.net/archive/2026.php#2026-11-18-1 (PHP Security Team release announcement)
- Vendor Advisory: https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-qc49-hpvq-g2w6 (PHP-FPM request smuggling to RCE; detailed technical write-up)

Supporting:
- Technical Analysis: https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-8mjj-2r7p-4hg2 (Magic method backtrace use-after-free; describes the demonstrated RCE chain)
- Technical Analysis: https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-2fjv-p558-g82m (Fatal-error backtrace use-after-free after shutdown)
- Technical Analysis: https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-gr4f-wgx5-jpfv (Timezone cache use-after-free; details of the FPM and mod_php exploits)
- Technical Analysis: https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-fm2m-fjf5-v3cp (Partially overwritten session files to RCE)
- Technical Analysis: https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-658j-r8rw-q6mx (Session serializer mismatch; gadget-chain RCE details)
- Technical Analysis: https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-g3vh-838c-65v7 (Interrupted session shutdown use-after-free)
- Technical Analysis: https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-jm4m-qfqx-967m (PHP-FPM epoll use-after-free; root exploit methodology)
- News Coverage: https://www.heise.de/news/Sicherheitsfix-PHP-Admins-bekommen-Donnerstagnachmittag-zu-tun-11530253.html
- News Coverage (English): https://www.heise.de/en/news/Security-patch-PHP-admins-have-work-to-do-Thursday-afternoon-11530262.html

*Timestamp of the Information: 19.11.2026, 15:56*
summary: The PHP project has released security updates for all supported branches of the PHP scripting language. Several flaws are rated critical and can lead to remote code execution in non-default or uncommon setups. The most serious is a PHP-FPM request smuggling flaw that lets an unauthenticated attacker run PHP code without memory corruption. Others include use-after-free bugs in the engine and session handling, plus a local privilege escalation to root in PHP-FPM.
